title: AI risk: questions for the board
intro: Use these questions when management proposes a new AI system, expands an existing one, or reports on cyber risk. None needs a technical background to ask.
questions: Where do we use AI today, and who owns each use?
What business benefit are we seeking from this AI?
What actions can it take, such as sending messages, changing records or making payments?
Which actions require a person's approval, and can that approval be bypassed?
What could materially harm our customers or the business?
Have our websites and systems been tested against attackers who use AI, even where we do not use AI ourselves?
What has been tested, and what remains unknown?
What evidence do we need before launch or expansion?
Who can pause the system if something goes wrong?
sentence: Before approving this deployment, we need evidence of what the system can access and do, how approvals are enforced, what testing found, and who owns the remaining risks.
footnote: A scoped assessment gives evidence about what was tested, under the conditions tested. It does not guarantee future safety, find every weakness or establish compliance on its own.
